sources.title: Airline Industry: Potential Mergers and Acquisitions Driven by Financial and Competitive Pressures
sources.status: Retained for transparency after proxy rejection
sources.limitations: Passenger airlines were rejected as the primary analogue for sovereign institutional consolidation.

sources.title: Airline Mergers: Issues Raised by the Proposed Merger of American Airlines and US Airways
sources.supports: Observed concentration and competition considerations in airline mergers.
sources.status: Retained for transparency after proxy rejection
sources.limitations: Regulated airline merger dynamics do not calibrate sovereign loss of autonomy.

sources.title: Airline Competition: The Average Number of Competitors Serving the Majority of Passengers Has Changed Little
sources.supports: Counterevidence on how merger counts translate into passenger-market competition.
sources.limitations: Market-route competition differs from top-level institutional sovereignty and permanent subordination.

sources.title: It’s Official: The World Order Has Broken Down
sources.coverage: Dalio’s current interpretation of the external-order Big Cycle
sources.supports: Dalio states that the world is in Stage 6 of his Big Cycle, characterized by great disorder, weakened rules, and a clash of great powers.
sources.modelUse: Interpretive support for the authored current-wave scenario
sources.status: Current-cycle interpretation by the framework’s author; not empirical wave detection
sources.limitations: The Big Cycle is an interpretive framework. This source does not estimate consolidation severity, a 2029 resolution date, or an Apex transition probability.
